body:
The approved #669 rollout reviewed `Magnesium_Chloride` against `Mgcl2_X_6_H2o` before considering a merge. Both currently use CHEBI:86345 and hexahydrate chemistry, but the generic history contains both anhydrous CAS 7786-30-3 from name lookup and hexahydrate CAS 7791-18-6 from supplier data, later resolved through the selected target.

The captured supplier CSV line 275 associates generic aliases with M2670, and [Sigma M2670](https://www.sigmaaldrich.com/US/en/product/sial/m2670) explicitly identifies MgCl2·6H2O / 7791-18-6 / 203.30 g/mol. This establishes that product, not every generic recipe occurrence. The inspected current generic-label cohort lacks supplier/CAS/chemistry fields that would settle the whole source scope. ChEBI [6636](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:6636) and [86345](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/api/ontologies/chebi/terms?obo_id=CHEBI:86345) both carry the common magnesium chloride name despite distinct forms. Supplier evidence is an inspected web extraction; the historical formulation reference is a lead, not a verified formulation.

Decision for the bounded rollout: SUPPRESS `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` only on `MIM:Magnesium_Chloride / skos:exactMatch / CHEBI:86345`, retaining both YAML records, histories and chemistry. Keep the separate anhydrous `Mgcl2 / CHEBI:6636` owner and row unchanged. Do not merge or infer hydration for all generic sources.

Recommendation: keep the form decision open here. Trace original products/formulations or approve an evidence-backed naming convention before a merge. A later merge must preserve #414 provenance and rejected aliases, choose the surviving owner explicitly and union overlapping memberships rather than adding counts. Native receipts and fresh review remain required. #868 already routes this magnesium identity concern to #811; this comment does not expand the current curation scope.

Observation at the assigned frozen MIM baseline `e000d66dd26ab053e9b17ce7bf8d3c873c3dde99` (explicit dependency PR #1158), with isolated proposals. This is not a claim about a later main revision.

`data/ingredients/mapped/Alk_So42.yaml` still carries `Na SiO .9H O` and `ZnSO .7H O` as resolving `EXACT_SYNONYM` values on CHEBI:86463 potassium aluminium sulfate. Their sodium/silicon and zinc formula fragments do not denote that aluminium/potassium sulfate identity. The defect does not require guessing a complete intended hydrate formula for either malformed string.

The independently reviewed isolated `a-proposal-anhydrous-alum` retypes both values to `REJECTED_LABEL`, preserving exact source text and provenance, while adding a separately source-supported explicitly anhydrous alias. Baseline SHA256: `eb7149b3301b2f405c59d0463b04bf6db774703bb3e914d125ffe9086ac717ed`; proposed SHA256: `8b74660fe96d2e9cc2eaeb36ad1e995a6d86f548f817041541959f754f2c60ce`. C166 and the exact proposal bytes were independently reviewed by B in `b/review-a/additional-review-c166.json`.

Preserve `SEM:15761b556078b9a904a8` and `reports/yaml_record_review/Alk_So42.md`. That historical finding also covers CultureMech metadata strings, so rejection of the two foreign fragments does not close the whole finding or approve the entire owner. The older #529 duplicate-synonym issue and #662 confidence-table issue concern different defects and are not substitutes for this existing #811 entry.

Follow-up: guarded integration, withdrawal of inherited support for changed bytes, final full-owner review, and coordinator-controlled synchronization so these values remain provenance-only and do not resolve or enter published `other`. No source ingredient is reassigned to a guessed sodium silicate or zinc sulfate hydrate, no occurrence count is changed, and no downstream rebuild has run in this source-review campaign.

W08-IR-008 independently confirms four remaining resolving phosphate aliases in complete selected payloads at `b90a2fd4681d20e2586481b7b9b1114a78281b94`. The existing generic Potassium phosphate concern applies directly; the malformed formula examples belong to the same bounded owner review.

| Owner | Still-resolving strings | Exact selected payload SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| K2hpo4.yaml / CHEBI:131527 | `KH2HPO4`, `K2HPO` | `6bd2194c63c815c81750a6e61e6da8d85db6579ebeee15626caf1328bbc645a4` |
| Kh2po4.yaml / CHEBI:63036 | `KH PO`, `Potassium Phosphate` | `3d0229f92f67f101f4af0975821cbd5ba4e26145c0d8b7f9f5d19ca395708b27` |

The native synonym function resolves all four. Preserve literal text/history/source credit as REJECTED_LABEL unless a precise primary correction supports a narrower occurrence-bound use. Do not silently transfer source memberships or assume a typo determines a chemical identity. Keep the valid anhydrous-base spelling and prior1215 concentration-alias corrections;1216 molybdate is a separate scope. These are unapplied proposal repairs needing new exact-byte independent review.
